topic: Hancock gambled her Warlord seat on one kick at Smoker in chapter 560
title: Hancock Bet Her Warlord Seat On One Kick
description: In chapter 560, Hancock snapped Smoker's jitte while he warned her about her Warlord status. I think that kick was a real gamble, not a joke. Was she bluffing or sure?
comment: Was Hancock bluffing about her beauty saving her Warlord seat, or did she know the Navy needed her? Pick one.

lines.text: Hancock's kick at Smoker was the riskiest thing a Warlord did all war.

shot.fallback: empress kicking a smoky marine officer

lines.text: Chapter 559. Smoker has Luffy pinned under his Seastone jitte.

shot.fallback: marine with two cigars pinning a boy

lines.text: Hancock kicks him off, and her Haki lets her touch a Logia.

shot.fallback: black haki kick hitting a smoke man

lines.text: He asks why a Warlord isn't doing her duty. She doesn't even answer.
Then in chapter 560 she snaps his jitte in half with Perfume Femur.
Smoker warns her the Navy may take her Warlord title.
She answers that her beauty will keep it safe. That's the line everyone laughs at.
Mihawk, Kuma, Moria and Doflamingo were all standing right there. She was replaceable.

shot.search: Warlords Marineford Mihawk Doflamingo Moria Hancock
shot.fallback: row of warlords on a war field

lines.text: So that was a real bet, and I think she knew it when her foot swung.

shot.fallback: empress standing in front of a boy

lines.text: Her island's shield was the price tag, and she paid it for Luffy.
But the title wasn't the only thing she put on the line for him.

shot.fallback: empress walking beside a boy in a straw hat

lines.text: Hancock's kick at Smoker was the riskiest thing a Warlord did, and it wasn't even her biggest bet.

shot.fallback: empress mid kick with a fierce look

self_check.hook: Line 1 names Hancock and claims the kick was a gamble.
self_check.loop: Last line restates the opening claim and flows back into line 1.
